title: Block future keys with a causal mask
description: A quick reference for lower-triangular visibility, prefix normalization, shifted decoder inputs, and position boundaries used here.

terms.definition: An attention visibility rule allowing each query to use its own key and all earlier keys, but no later keys.
The rule that keeps each query's same-position input key inside the allowed lower triangle.
A score-space mask adding zero to allowed cells and negative infinity to future cells before softmax.
One row of attention scores associated with a single query position.
One column of attention scores associated with a single candidate key position.
The current position and all earlier key positions over which a query's probabilities are normalized.
A key later than the current query position whose attention probability is exactly zero.
Row normalization performed only across the allowed prefix, assigning exact zero to blocked cells.
A training input offset by one target position so the allowed diagonal contains an earlier known token, not the predicted target.
The property that changing future keys and values cannot change any earlier attention output.
Separate absolute or relative information that distinguishes token order; the causal mask provides visibility, not position.
